claims.text: Integrating machine-learning potentials with DFT calculations could improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The integrated approach could improve determination of fusion enthalpy.
The integrated approach could improve determination of fusion entropy.
The integrated approach could improve determination of the volume change at the transition.
The integrated approach could improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
Chemical short-range order and its evolution act as the structural mediator for the proposed improvement.
Chemical short-range order can evolve in a refractory high-entropy alloy and measurably alter a material property.
Combining machine-learning potentials with DFT better captures complex interactions in multicomponent systems.
Better capture of complex interactions enhances the accuracy of thermodynamic-property predictions.
Combining machine-learning potentials with DFT enhances computational efficiency.
The proposed approach is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy materials in high-temperature states.
The extent of improvement depends on the quality and integration of the machine-learning potentials and DFT methods and on the material's compositional and structural complexity.

The proposal can be tested by comparing its predicted transition temperature, fusion quantities, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity against experimental measurements for a selected multicomponent high-entropy material.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
